html:
The Pandyas were one of the three old Tamil royal houses of southern India, ruling from Madurai. The map shows their state in 800 and 900, and again from 1279 to 1400.

They appear in Sangam poems and Greek and Roman sources as one of the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas. Their history in the map's years has two peaks:

  • First Pandya empire (about 590 to 920): after a dark age, Pandya kings revived and fought the Pallavas and Sri Lanka. In the early 900s the Cholas conquered them.
  • Second Pandya empire (1216 to the 1300s): as Chola power collapsed, the Pandyas became the strongest state in the south. Jatavarman Sundara Pandya (1251 to 1268) ruled from the Kaveri to Sri Lanka. Marco Polo visited the Pandya coast around 1292 and described its pearl fisheries and its horse trade with Arabia.

A civil war between two princes opened the way for the Delhi general Malik Kafur, who raided Madurai in 1311. The Madurai Sultanate ruled there from 1335 until Vijayanagara took it in 1378. Pandya princes lived on as local chiefs in the far south.
sum: The Pandyas were one of the three old Tamil royal houses of southern India, ruling from Madurai. The map shows their state in 800 and 900, and again from 1279 to 1400.
